subject: ventures/caa-record-check
professional: a PKI / certificate-operations engineer (CA/B Forum practitioner) who writes and debugs CAA policy and knows RFC 8659 section 3 processing by heart

evidence.correctness: Ran node check.mjs letsencrypt.org --ca pki.goog live through the DoH resolver: returned the real record set (issue amazon.com, letsencrypt.org, pki.goog, sectigo.com ...), so the live path works. Recomputed with a scratch script against RFC 8659/8657/3597: (1) RFC 3597 generic-hex of '0 issue "letsencrypt.org"' built by hand decodes to the right flag/tag/value; (2) flag 128 is critical, 'issue' with critical bit is not flagged unknown but '128 tbs' is: correct; (3) RFC 8657 value 'letsencrypt.org; accounturi=...; validationmethods=dns-01' parses to issuer plus both parameters: correct; (4) issuewild ";" with issue letsencrypt.org gives non-wildcard authorized, wildcard disallow-all: matches RFC 8659 4.3; (5) issuewild-only set gives non-wildcard open and wildcard restricted: correct. WRONG: RFC 8659 section 3 says R(X)=CAA(X), else CAA(A(X)) for the alias target only, else R(P(X)) climbing from the ORIGINAL name's parent. The tool instead replaces the name with the CNAME target and climbs the target's ancestors. Reproduced: blog.example.com CNAME host.example.net., no CAA at either, example.com has 'issue digicert.com' -> tool reports foundAtName null, walked host.example.net/example.net/net, i.e. 'no CAA anywhere, any CA may issue'; RFC says only digicert.com may issue. CNAMEs at ancestors during the climb are also never consulted (a.b.example.com with b.example.com CNAME x.other.org gives null). A false 'authorized' is the dangerous direction. Also 'RFC 3597 presentation' unquoted values ('0 issue letsencrypt.org') are reported MALFORMED. Other outputs right, one logic path wrong, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim: tree-walk to first ancestor with CAA works (lookup.test + live); issuewild fallback works; critical-unknown flag works; RFC 8657 parameter parsing works; both wire formats (presentation and generic hex) decode; 8-CA shortlist plus arbitrary --ca works (CLI run); exit codes 0/1/2 coded as stated (usage error exits 2, verified); --json works by reading; browser page present with hostname and CA fields and two explainer pages exist. No stubs or TODOs found. Parameters (accounturi/validationmethods) are parsed but never used in the verdict, so an account-restricted issue record still reads 'authorized: named' (README does not claim otherwise). Not browser-run in this session (no browser), page logic read only. Single CNAME hop is acknowledged in source comments, but its tree-climb semantics are the defect above.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/caa-record-check && node --test '*.test.mjs': 73 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation in analyze.mjs (wildcardAuthorized: issuewild.length > 0 changed to > 99, disabling the issuewild override): 2 tests failed (issuewild overrides issue; issuewild ';' disallows wildcard). Reverted with git checkout; suite back to 73 pass and git status clean. Weaknesses: the lookup test 'follows a single CNAME hop before walking for CAA' enshrines the non-RFC behaviour, so tests would not catch the CNAME defect; no test for unquoted presentation values; no network integration test (resolver is injected fake only); only one mutation tried.
evidence.craft: Read parse.mjs, analyze.mjs, lookup.mjs, check.mjs. Zero-dependency ESM shared by CLI and browser, injected resolver for testing, timeouts and AbortController, resolver errors surfaced not swallowed (good). Defects: verdictForCustomCa duplicates verdictFor's decision chain as nested ternaries (two copies of the rule engine, drift risk); parse.mjs tag check '!knownTags.has && !/^[a-z0-9-]+$/' is effectively dead (presentation regex already enforces it); no hostname normalisation (https://example.com/path or *.example.com is queried verbatim, walking 'com/path'); check.mjs parseArgs silently ignores unknown --flags and treats a value-less --ca as undefined; the lookup docstring contains an unfinished stream-of-consciousness sentence about empty record sets. Competent overall.
evidence.claims: Checked: README 'tree-walk per RFC 8659' and 'computed the way RFC 8659 says a CA must compute it' backed for the plain climb, NOT for CNAME (index.html JSON-LD line 25 and lookup.mjs docstring state alias handling that is wrong per RFC). 'Never contacts the hostname' backed by lookup.mjs (only dohQuery to cloudflare-dns.com). Privacy claims backed by usage.mjs/usage.test.mjs. Disclaimer/no-warranty present in README and page. KNOWN_CAS honestly labelled non-exhaustive. Cloudflare DoH changelog 2026-07-28 claim could not be verified offline. Artifact problems: sitemap.xml and canonical use example.invalid and llms.txt links point to a github.io host (CLAUDE.md says the catalogue is served at marisstella.app); llms.txt carries the boilerplate 'estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial' line that does not fit a DNS checker. Checks the correctness defect on a headline claim, so 2.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a sysadmin whose subdomain cert fails to renew pastes the hostname and a CA domain, gets the governing record set, the ancestor it came from, per-CA wildcard/non-wildcard verdicts and critical-tag diagnosis; live CLI run completed in seconds with readable text and CI-usable exit codes. Plain subdomain-under-parent case (the headline job) works. Gaps that would bite in the first hour for CNAME-hosted subdomains (very common for SaaS-hosted subdomains) and for account-bound issue records.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 8659 section 3 (processing algorithm) and 4.2-4.3, RFC 8657 and RFC 3597. Tree-climb, issuewild fallback, critical-bit semantics, disallow-all and parameter grammar match. Departs on: alias handling (checks only the first-name CNAME and climbs from the target, where RFC checks CAA(A(X)) exactly and climbs from P(X)); no DNAME or ancestor-CNAME handling; ignores accounturi/validationmethods in the verdict; does not note that a CA must treat unrecognised issue parameters specially or that DNSSEC-bogus answers (SERVFAIL) block issuance (it does surface RCODE errors). A PKI engineer would accept the climb and reject the alias handling.

defects.what: CNAME handling departs from RFC 8659 section 3: tool climbs from the CNAME target's ancestors instead of checking only CAA(target) and then climbing from the original name's parent. A CNAME-hosted subdomain under a restrictive parent is reported 'no CAA anywhere, any CA may issue'. The lookup test encodes the wrong behaviour.
CNAMEs at ancestor labels during the climb (and DNAME) are never consulted; only the typed name gets a CNAME query.
Unquoted presentation-format values ('0 issue letsencrypt.org') are rejected as MALFORMED and surface as findings; no hostname normalisation (URL or wildcard input queried verbatim).
Verdict ignores accounturi/validationmethods restrictions; an account-bound issue record reads 'authorized: named' without caveat.
sitemap.xml and canonical use example.invalid, llms.txt links a github.io host and carries tax/legal boilerplate irrelevant to a DNS tool.
verdictForCustomCa duplicates the verdictFor rule chain; dead tag-regex condition; unfinished sentence in resolveCaaSet docstring.

verdict: A tidy, zero-dependency, honestly caveated CAA checker whose 73 tests pass, whose live CLI run returned the real record set, and whose core processing (issuewild fallback, critical flag, RFC 8657 parameters, generic-hex decoding) I recomputed correctly, with a seeded mutation caught by 2 tests. It does not meet the bar: its alias (CNAME) handling contradicts RFC 8659 section 3, producing a false 'any CA may issue' for CNAME-hosted subdomains beneath a restrictive parent, and that error is advertised on the page as RFC-conformant and locked in by a test. Finished (completeness 3) but correctness and claims are 2, so not at the senior-practitioner level yet. The fix is small: query CAA(X), then CAA(A(X)) without climbing, then climb from the original name's parents.
